title: The Hollow Ember
premise: Cyrus Sandoval has spent her life copying scripture in a valley where magic cannot cross the border, paying down a family debt she never incurred. When tonight's exact date surfaces in a century-old prophecy, she is seized by the temple's wardens and dragged beyond the valley's edge into a kingdom ruled by a king whose crown is slowly devouring him. Guided by a disgraced prophecy-scholar and the king's exiled sister, Cyrus discovers the ember of magic inside herself — the first spark the valley's founders hid away — and learns the prophecy demands a scribe's hand, not a hero's. To free the king, she must rewrite the prophecy itself, trading her memories of everyone she loves as the ink. She succeeds, saving the kingdom but returning to the valley as a stranger to her own past, holding one blank page that might let her begin again.
about_author: L. M. Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing damaged manuscripts before turning to fiction. They write about people who inherit debts they never chose, and live in a house full of unfinished books.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Cyrus, a temple scribe, copies scripture by candlelight while tallying her family's crushing debt; a minor act of curiosity — reading a forbidden prophecy folio — reveals tonight's date in century-old ink. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: restless longing beneath a life of obedient smallness, and the first chill of being seen by fate.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Keep
chapters.summary: Temple wardens arrest Cyrus at dawn; the high priest reveals the prophecy names a 'scribe of the hollow valley' and the law requires her removal beyond the border where magic waits. Her mother's farewell is cold, transactional — the debt transfers to a cousin. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal by the only home she's known, grief disguised as duty.

chapters.title: The Border of Ash
chapters.summary: Crossing the valley's edge, Cyrus feels magic flood back into a world that has been mute her whole life — and it recognizes her, sparking painfully in her fingertips. She is delivered to the capital, a city of gilded rot, and meets Vess, a disgraced prophecy-scholar who claims the text is unfinished. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: terror and intoxication entwined; she has power she never asked for.

chapters.title: A Crown That Eats Its Wearer
chapters.summary: Cyrus glimpses King Aldric at court: young, hollow-eyed, with something ancient moving behind his face. Vess explains the crown is a parasite — a bound spirit feeding on the king's memories — and the prophecy's scribe is the only one who can unbind it. POV: Cyrus, with a brief interlude in Aldric's fading memories. Emotional beat: pity curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: The King's Sister in Exile
chapters.summary: Princess Isolde, exiled for accusing the crown of sorcery years ago, tests Cyrus's spark and teaches her the old binding-craft — but wants the king dead, not saved, and says so. Cyrus refuses; Isolde warns the crown will use her mercy. First assassination attempt on Cyrus, barely survived. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: alliance built on distrust, the cost of compassion named aloud.

chapters.title: Ink, Blood, and Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Studying the prophecy's original manuscript, Cyrus finds marginalia in her grandmother's handwriting — her family's debt was payment for hiding the valley's stolen ember inside a bloodline: hers. The crown's agents burn Vess's archive; Vess is gravely wounded shielding the book. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as both wound and weapon; fury at being a pawn across generations.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: Cyrus confronts Aldric privately; the crown-spirit speaks through him, offering to erase her debt and her memories of loss if she abandons the unbinding. She sees the real king flicker beneath — a boy who once loved the valley. She refuses, and the spirit marks her for death. POV: Cyrus, with a haunting passage in the spirit's voice. Emotional beat: temptation faced and survived, at the price of being hunted.

chapters.title: What We Bury to Survive
chapters.summary: Fleeing to the valley's border, Cyrus and Isolde reconcile partially; Isolde admits her exile was self-chosen shame, and lends her the ritual knife. Cyrus learns the unbinding requires rewriting the prophecy in her own blood — and the ink's price is every memory she holds dear. She begins choosing which ones to keep. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; love measured in what she is willing to forget.

chapters.title: The Hollow Ember
chapters.summary: In the throne room, Cyrus begins the rewriting as the crown-spirit unleashes the court's possessed guards; Isolde holds the line, wounded. Cyrus bleeds the new ending into the folio, surrendering her memories — her mother's face, Vess's laugh, the valley itself — as the spirit is unbound and Aldric collapses, freed and weeping. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: climax of sacrifice; triumph indistinguishable from loss.

chapters.title: A Blank Page
chapters.summary: Cyrus wakes in the valley, debt-forgiven by a king she cannot remember, her past a fog with one blank page in her satchel. Vess finds her, a stranger, and begins telling her their story from the beginning; on the last page, her hand moves as if it remembers. POV: Cyrus, closing with Vess's voice. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal — memory lost, but the self that chose love endures.
